title: clean_test_db.py orphan-tenant DELETE silently no-ops: WinGet psql.CMD shim drops -c SQL argument on this host
summary: While resolving an ADHOC zig build test-env-verify C4 schema-baseline failure (109 orphaned public.tenant rows with storage_mode='SCHEMA' and no matching tenant_schemas/Postgres schema on the shared db_test container, port 5434), verify_schema_baseline.py --auto-fix was confirmed (by reading its source first) to only re-apply the GBL-133 iss0112 schema-ledger-reconcile migration -- additive/idempotent, backfills public.schema_migrations ledger rows only, never creates tenant schemas or touches public.tenant rows -- so it could not and did not fix this failure mode (confirmed by running it: applied cleanly, 0 rows changed in public.tenant, drift unchanged). The correct remediation path is tools/clean_test_db.py's GH-443/ISS-0140 orphan-tenant DELETE (lines ~408-412: DELETE FROM public.tenant WHERE storage_mode='SCHEMA' AND slug != 'default' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.tenant_schemas ...)), which zig build test-env-verify's C4 check already invokes automatically as a self-heal pre-step per ISS-0605/GH-537. However running `python tools/clean_test_db.py` directly reported 'Test database cleaned.' (exit 0) but did NOT remove the 109 orphan rows -- confirmed by re-running verify_schema_baseline.py --check-tenants immediately after, which still reported all 109 missing. Root-caused: clean_test_db.py's run_psql() resolves psql via shutil.which('psql'), which on this host resolves to a WinGet-installed shim (C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WinGet\Links\psql.CMD) that does NOT forward its -c '<SQL>' argument to the underlying psql.exe -- every -c invocation (regardless of the SQL string, including a deliberately-invalid column reference) silently returns a fixed '?column? / 1' output (the shape of a bare SELECT 1) and exit code 0. Reproduced via subprocess.run with an explicit argv list (no shell involved), so this is not a shell-quoting artifact -- the shim itself drops the -c payload. This means every mutating run_psql() call in clean_test_db.py (DELETE/TRUNCATE) silently no-ops while the script reports success, masking every cleanup failure on any host where this WinGet shim resolves first. --version and no-argument invocations of the shim work correctly, which is why this had not surfaced before.

root_cause.details: shutil.which('psql') resolves to a WinGet Links .cmd shim (not the real psql.exe) on this host. The shim does not correctly forward a '-c' flag with a SQL-string argument through to the wrapped psql.exe -- confirmed via direct subprocess.run(['<shim path>', db_url, '-c', 'SELECT 42']) returning '1' instead of '42', and via subprocess.run([..., '-c', 'SELECT this_is_not_a_real_column FROM public.tenant']) returning the same '?column? / 1' with exit 0 instead of a column-does-not-exist error -- proving the shim never actually executes the passed SQL. clean_test_db.py's GH-280/ISS-0040 comment block already documents this exact shim's existence and why shutil.which() was introduced (to resolve the .cmd extension at all on Windows), but did not anticipate that the resolved shim could itself be non-functional for -c invocations while still succeeding for --version.

resolution.details: Not fixed as part of this ADHOC handoff (out of scope; task was the test-env-verify blocker, not this tooling script). Workaround applied to unblock: ran the exact orphan-tenant DELETE SQL from clean_test_db.py lines 408-412 verbatim via `docker exec r-co-db_test-1 psql -U bpm -d bpm_test -c "..."` (the container's own real psql, bypassing the broken host-side shim entirely), which removed the 109 orphan rows with no other data changes. Suggested fix directions (for the assignee, not evaluated in depth): (1) add a self-check probe in clean_test_db.py's psql-resolution logic that sends a non-1 sentinel value (e.g. SELECT 424242, since SELECT 1 cannot distinguish real execution from this shim's fallback) and falls back to an alternate resolution strategy if the probe fails; (2) switch clean_test_db.py's mutating statements to psycopg2 (already a hard dependency of tools/verify_schema_baseline.py) instead of shelling out to psql, removing the shim-resolution problem entirely; (3) audit other tools/*.py scripts for the same shutil.which('psql') + '-c' pattern.

verification: Reproduced deterministically 3 times via subprocess.run with explicit argv (no shell interpretation) using both a valid distinguishing query (SELECT 42 -> returns 1) and a deliberately-invalid query (SELECT this_is_not_a_real_column FROM public.tenant -> returns 1 with exit 0, no error) against the resolved shim path C:\Users\tvolo\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WinGet\Links\psql.CMD. Confirmed the workaround DELETE (run directly via docker exec against the container's own psql) actually removed the 109 rows: verify_schema_baseline.py --check-tenants went from FAIL (109 missing) to all-OK/PASS immediately after, and zig build test-env-verify went from UNHEALTHY at C4 to HEALTHY (10/10 checks PASS, exit 0) with no other intervention.
prevention: Any tool that shells out to a resolved executable path via shutil.which() and trusts a mutating -c/-e/-x style flag to have actually executed should self-verify with a distinguishing (non-trivially-guessable) sentinel value before trusting subsequent success-implying exit codes, especially on Windows where PATH resolution can land on a third-party shim (WinGet, Scoop, npm global shims) instead of the real binary.

A script that reports success ('Test database cleaned.', exit 0) after a sequence of run_psql() calls whose individual return values are discarded (see clean_test_db.py lines 394-395, 408-412: run_psql(...) called without checking its bool return) cannot distinguish 'the SQL ran and matched 0 rows' from 'the SQL never ran at all' -- both look identical to the caller. Checking (and surfacing) run_psql()'s return value at every call site would have caught this immediately rather than requiring a manual row-count re-check.
